# --instructions--

Create a class `Settings` with `var theme: String` starting at `"light"` and `var fontSize: Int` starting at `12`.

Then write a function `makeSettings(name: String?, size: Int): Settings` that returns a `Settings()` configured with `apply`, where `fontSize` is always set to `size` and `theme` is set to `name` only when `name` is not `null`, using `?.let`.

Example: `makeSettings(null, 14)` keeps the theme `light`.

# --asserts--

`makeSettings("dark", 16)` must have theme `dark` and font size `16`

```kotlin
    val dark = makeSettings("dark", 16)
    tryCatch(dark.theme == "dark" && dark.fontSize == 16)
```

`makeSettings(null, 14)` must keep the default theme `light`

```kotlin
    tryCatch(makeSettings(null, 14).theme == "light")
```

`makeSettings(null, 14)` must still set the font size to `14`

```kotlin
    tryCatch(makeSettings(null, 14).fontSize == 14)
```

A new `Settings()` must start with theme `light` and font size `12`

```kotlin
    val fresh = Settings()
    tryCatch(fresh.theme == "light" && fresh.fontSize == 12)
```

# --solutions--

```kotlin
class Settings {
    var theme: String = "light"
    var fontSize: Int = 12
}

fun makeSettings(name: String?, size: Int): Settings {
    return Settings().apply {
        fontSize = size
        name?.let { theme = it }
    }
}
```
